result.title: Same Error, Different Recovery: How Delivery Changes LLM Agent Behavior
result.summary: A tool-using language model must decide whether to retry a failed call, correct it, or stop and tell the user. The error text alone may not be enough: the same feedback can lead to different actions depending on where it appears in the conversation. We isolate this delivery problem by varying placement, guidance, retained history and turn structure. Two studies with plans fixed before data collection, across 13 open models from 3B to 70B parameters, compare the next action and subsequent task completion, with exact deterministic reruns. A new user turn that retains the failed exchange avoids the severe stopping failure observed in Llama models when that exchange is removed. It is non-inferior to history rewriting in pooled synthetic comparisons, but is not best for every model. We implement this form as an opt-in recovery layer within a deterministic inference engine and evaluate it on public benchmarks and a coding agent. On ToolMaze, it raises success on explicit errors by 14.2 points with 7-8B models and 10.5 points with 32-70B models; Loud/Quiet, 24 multi-turn tasks with visible failures and silent corruption, scored by final-state agreement, shows no measurable gain. A client given the exact fault kind performs better still. The findings support delivery as a distinct factor in recovery, not an engine-exclusive solution or a universal retry policy.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文以工具调用失败后的下一步动作为对象，在13个开源模型上系统改变错误反馈的放置位置、引导、保留历史与轮次结构，并在确定性推理引擎中实现一种「新用户轮」式的恢复层，在ToolMaze与编码agent上测试恢复成功率。
AI.relevance_reason: 其对「重试/纠正/停止」三类动作的因果拆分与反馈投递形式，可能为LVR中STOP决策、证据回填位置如何影响后续推理状态提供可核查线索，但研究对象为纯文本工具agent，无视觉状态，迁移需自行验证。
